title: Port is not opened on keepers only using composable protocols
body:
**Description**
When using the composable protocols configuration for serving prometheus metrics with tls, clickhouse server with only keeper configuration does not open specified port.

**How to reproduce**
* Clickhouse version 23.3.19.32

To reproduce the issue two nodes should be deployed, one as "data" node and the other one as a keeper.
Example config:
```xml
<remote_servers>
<example>
  <shard>
    <internal_replication>true</internal_replication>
    <replica>
      <host>data-node.example.com</host>
      <port>9000</port>
      <secure>true</secure>
    </replica>
  </shard>
</example>
</remote_servers>

<keeper_server>
  <server_id>1</server_id>
  <tcp_port_secure>2181</tcp_port_secure>
  <raft_configuration>
      <secure>true</secure>

      <server>
          <id>1</id>
          <hostname>keeper-node.example.com</hostname>
          <port>2182</port>
      </server>
  </raft_configuration>
</keeper_server>


```

In both configs I do specify prometheus metrics endpoint using composable protocols following explanation given in this issue #49003:
```xml
<prometheus>
  <endpoint>/metrics</endpoint>
  <metrics>true</metrics>
  <events>true</events>
  <asynchronous_metrics>true</asynchronous_metrics>
</prometheus>

<protocols>
  <prometheus_protocol>
      <type>prometheus</type>
      <description>prometheus protocol</description>
  </prometheus_protocol>

  <prometheus_secure>
      <type>tls</type>
      <impl>prometheus_protocol</impl>
      <port>9999</port>
      <description>prometheus over tls</description>
  </prometheus_secure>
</protocols>

```


**Expected behavior**
Port 9999 is opened on both "data" node and keeper node and is under TLS.

**Actual behavior**
Port 9999 is only opened on the "data" and not the keeper node.

**Logs**
There were no messages in log with a mention of this prometheus configuration, checked it on trace level.
author: ilyatrefilov

comments.body: Keeper currently doesn't support composable protocols so the "old" way should be used of specifying `<port>` under `<prometheus>`.

@ilyatrefilov I can't promise you anything specific but I think it should be done in the near future along with some small changes to Keeper prometheus metrics (send only Keeper specific data).

I'll close this issue for now and ping you when there is update for it.

title: OOM on group by query
author: rikuiki

comments.body: Alexey, maybe you have a chance to comment why do you think it is not a potential bug?..

memory limit currently strictly limits only pre aggregation phase (separate aggregation on execution threads). at the time of merging we need to bring smth around `total_aggr_state_size * aggregation_memory_efficient_merge_threads / NUM_BUCKETS (=256)` into memory. and you got error at merging phase as you see.
as a workaround you could try to lower `aggregation_memory_efficient_merge_threads` if increasing memory limit is not an option.
#40588 is aimed to address this issue 
P.S. it is not a good idea to set `max_bytes_before_external_group_by` too low. the lower this setting the more intermediate files will be generated. apart from consuming time it also affect memory usage in a bad way: for reading these files we will allocate 1MB buffer for each of them. you could easily get hundreds or even thousands of such small files with really small `max_bytes_before_external_group_by`. good default value is half of the memory limit.

Thank you for explanation!

> it is not a good idea to set max_bytes_before_external_group_by too low. 

I did this just for testing purposes, to check if ClickHouse can handle aggregation when data doesn't fit into memory, and reduced it even more when seen OOM.

title: ParsingException when importing Point data from CSV
body:
When importing CSV files with geo Point data, I always get this error:

> `Code: 27. DB::ParsingException: Cannot parse input: expected '"' before: '(10, 10)"'`

To reproduce the problem under simple conditions, I created a table with a Point column:
`CREATE TABLE default.geo_point (p Point) ENGINE = Memory()`

I also created a geo_point.csv file with a single point in it:
```
"(10, 10)"
```

I import the file with the clickhouse client (version 22.9.3.18) like this:
`cat geo_point.csv | clickhouse-client -q 'INSERT INTO default.geo_point FORMAT CSV'`

I get the above error, even when removing the double quotes. Not sure if this is a bug, or if I need to pass a certain flag to the clickhouse-client (I didn't find a flag that works). 

Other datatypes are imported just fine. Also, when I change the data type from Point to String, the import works fine.

Reproduces at 20.8.12.2 Clickhouse version.

The last statement falls into error: `Cannot execute replicated DDL query, maximum retires exceeded`

```
Code: 524. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9100. DB::Exception: ALTER of key column b from type Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2) to type Enum8('a' = 1) must be metadata-only.
```


**Expected behavior**
The same as on non-Replicated MergeTree
author: Blackmorse

comments.body:
Hi!

Alter of the key columns in ClickHouse is quite limited. You can alter enums but only add new values. Removing old values can change the representation of the primary key. 
```
:) ALTER TABLE t
    MODIFY COLUMN `b` Enum8('a' = 1)

Received exception from server (version 21.2.1):
Code: 524. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: ALTER of key column b from type Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2) to type Enum8('a' = 1) is not safe because it can change the representation of primary key. 
```
but the extension is allowed:
```

ALTER TABLE t
    MODIFY COLUMN `b` Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2, 'c' = 3)

Ok.

```

> The same as on non-Replicated MergeTree

But how it's related to Replicated / non-Replicated MergeTree?

@alesapin , 

>  You can alter enums but only add new values

But documentation says:

> The Enum type can be changed without cost using ALTER, if only the set of values is changed. It is possible to both add and remove members of the Enum using ALTER (removing is safe only if the removed value has never been used in the table)

> @alesapin ,
> 
> > You can alter enums but only add new values
> 
> But documentation says:
> 
> > The Enum type can be changed without cost using ALTER, if only the set of values is changed. It is possible to both add and remove members of the Enum using ALTER (removing is safe only if the removed value has never been used in the table)

As the documentation says:
`> removing is safe only if the removed value has never been used in the table`

We restrict unsafe operations for the primary key columns because it can lead not only to the single-column corruption but to the whole table became broken.
@alesapin , So , It is correct behaviour, right?

> @alesapin , So , It is correct behaviour, right?

Yes, it's expected, maybe we have to improve docs.
